claim.why_it_matters: D.19.5 is emitted at the same markdown level as its parent D.19, so it is promoted out of the Object-oriented-concepts subtree; every clause under it inherits the one-level shift. Sibling clauses of equal printed rank end up at two different markdown depths within the same annex clause.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds.

(1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claimed kind is 'missing-heading', but both headings are present verbatim. The 300dpi render of page 1142 prints, in bold, 'D.19.5   Other object oriented programming features' followed by the sentence 'Some of the other capabilities are Inheritance, Interfaces and Polymorphism, and Conformance.', then 'D.19.5.1   Inheritance'. The markdown at :45931 and :45936 carries both clause numbers and both titles character-for-character, plus correct anchors <a id="section-d-19-5"> and <a id="section-d-19-5-1">. Zero words of heading text are lost. The only delta is the count of '#' characters.

(2) THE PDF CONVEYS RANK BY CLAUSE NUMBER, NOT TYPOGRAPHY, AND THE NUMBER IS PRESERVED EXACTLY. On the rendered page, 'D.19.5' and 'D.19.5.1' are set in the same bold serif face at effectively the same size; the printed glyphs give no typographic rank cue distinguishing them. The claim's own premise -- 'D.19.5 printed at the same rank as D.19.1..D.19.4, D.19.5.1 one rank below' -- is an inference from the dotted numbering, not from anything the page prints. That numbering is reproduced intact in the markdown, so the hierarchy is fully recoverable and no meaning changes.

(3) MARKDOWN '#' DEPTH ENCODES NO HIERARCHY ANYWHERE IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION, so a depth mismatch cannot be a structural loss. Measured across the whole file: clause-depth-3 headings (e.g. D.19.5) are emitted as '##' 347 times, '###' 539 times, '####' 19 times; clause-depth-4 as '##' 241 / '###' 668 / '####' 32; clause-depth-5 as '##' 144 / '###' 151 / '####' 43. There is no mapping to invert. Page 1142 proves it locally: the running header is emitted as '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' (level 1, i.e. above the whole annex) and the page marker as '## Page 1142'. If '#' depth were a document tree, the running header would be the root of the standard. It is a flat per-page rendering, so the claimed 'promoted out of the subtree' consequence does not exist.

(4) IT IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE -- the exact category the protocol says to reject. Depth-3 clauses that are the FIRST heading after a '## Page NNNN' marker are emitted as '##' 251/279 times (90%); depth-3 clauses that are NOT first on a page are '##' only 96/626 times (15%). D.19.5 is the first heading on page 1142 (5 lines after the page marker). The transcriber resets heading depth at a page top; this is a document-wide page-boundary rendering artifact, identical in kind on hundreds of pages, not a page-1142 content defect.

ADDITIONALLY, THE CLAIM CITES SELECTIVELY. It offers '### D.19.1 General' and '### D.19.2 Classes' as the sibling baseline while omitting that the two nearest siblings are already '##': '## D.19.3 Objects' (:45637) and '## D.19.4 Methods' (:45795). Three of the five D.19.x siblings are '##'. So D.19.5 is not an outlier being singled out; it matches the majority of its own sibling set, and the '### D.19.1/D.19.2' pair is the minority. The framing 'sibling clauses of equal printed rank end up at two different markdown depths' is true of D.19.1/D.19.2 vs D.19.3/D.19.4 with no involvement of D.19.5 at all, which shows the observation is not about this heading or this page.

No text, no clause number, no ordering and no meaning differs between the PDF and the markdown on page 1142.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. Both page-1142 headings are transcribed completely and correctly ('D.19.5 Other object oriented programming features', 'D.19.5.1 Inheritance'), with correct clause numbers and anchors; nothing is missing, so the 'missing-heading' kind is factually wrong. The sole difference is the number of markdown '#' characters, which in this transcription is page-layout furniture rather than hierarchy: depth-3 clauses appearing first on a page are rendered '##' 90% of the time versus 15% otherwise, and D.19.5 is the first heading on page 1142. Across the file, '#' depth does not track clause depth in either direction (depth-3 clauses split 347/539/19 across ##/###/####), and page 1142 itself emits the running header at level 1 above everything, so no subtree relationship can be read out of '#' depth to be broken. If the ledger wants uniform heading depth it is a global, whole-file normalization task keyed off the dotted clause number, not a per-page content reconciliation finding, and it should not be recorded against page 1142.
